subject.title: Telegram delivery should be idempotent across message.send, final replies, and resumed turns

question: Should a successful Telegram message-tool send suppress only an equivalent final or recovery payload, or all later visible output for the logical turn?
rationale: The existing fixes intentionally distinguish duplicate replay from valid repeated answers; a general receipt design changes that user-visible delivery contract and cannot safely be inferred from this report alone.

options.title: Require equivalent-output proof
options.body: Keep existing scoped suppression and request a redacted current-main trace before designing any new receipt state.

options.title: Adopt turn-wide suppression
options.body: Define a durable logical-turn receipt that suppresses every later visible delivery, accepting the risk of hiding intentional follow-ups.

recommendation.title: Require equivalent-output proof
recommendation.body: Keep existing scoped suppression and request a redacted current-main trace before designing any new receipt state.

likelyOwner.reason: Their documented delivery-mirror change already establishes the closest equivalent-text-versus-repeated-answer boundary.
